title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop for the animal. This shows a perception or decision failure where the system either did not detect the duck as an obstacle or did not treat it as one warranting collision avoidance.

The failure occurred during public deployment in a neighborhood. It would have been caught by either a perception system that reliably detects small animals in the vehicle's path, or a decision layer that treats detected objects as obstacles regardless of size. Avride's response included simulation testing and adjusted its testing area, suggesting the company does not yet know with certainty why the system failed to avoid the duck.

It is not established what specific technical failure occurred, whether the perception system missed the duck or classified it as non-threatening, or whether similar incidents have happened in the broader fleet.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without stopping or slowing down. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, was familiar to residents, intensifying their concerns about autonomous vehicle technology in their area.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and investigated the situation by reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene in simulation. The company denied a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it made complete and appropriate stops at all relevant intersections. In response, Avride adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake. The company is now conducting controlled experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations without compromising overall safety performance. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.
